title: Shifting Right: y = f(x-3)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Starting from the graph of y=f(x), explain how the graph of y=f(x-3) is produced and where the point (2,5) of the original would land.

steps.title: Match the Inputs
steps.explanation: The new formula reproduces the old output f(a) at the larger input a+3, since (a+3)-3=a.
steps.why: Reading f(x-3) is asking the original function for the value three units to the left of x.

steps.title: State the Shift Direction
steps.explanation: Hence the entire graph slides 3 units to the right, with heights unchanged.
steps.why: Inside-the-function subtractions move the graph in the positive x direction, the opposite of the sign's first impression.

steps.title: Apply to the Sample Point
steps.explanation: The point (2,5) of y=f(x) moves to (5,5) on y=f(x-3).
steps.why: Adding 3 to the x-coordinate and keeping y is exactly the map from Step 2.

steps.title: Describe the Sketch
steps.explanation: Draw the same curve three units to the right; nothing stretches, flips, or changes height.
